_source: AI-researched venue CANDIDATES for Manchester and Cheshire, awaiting review — never directly edited by the research agent. Populated by a daily scheduled research agent (2026-08, at explicit user request: 'fan out some research agents who's goal is to run every day to find and suggest new businesses... they shouldn't go beyond cheshire and manchester just yet'; bumped from ~3-5/day to 10/day at a later explicit request). See .claude/agents/curia-research-daily.md for the full research brief/rules this agent works under (Hard rule 1 chain/fast-food screening, real coordinates only, no duplicates, Do/Drink/Eat coverage balance). The research agent commits straight to master for this file (no PR — this queue has zero effect on the live app, nothing reads it except the review agent and the admin dashboard's Growth Insights context). A second, independent daily agent (.claude/agents/curia-suggestion-review.md) re-verifies each `pending` entry and is the thing that promotes one into the real docs/data/venues.json, pushing straight to master after its own independent re-verification (see that file's own 2026-09-04 doc comment for why the human checkpoint moved to Curia Command's Pending Review tab instead of a PR here). Each entry mirrors docs/data/venues.json's own raw shape (name/district/type/spend/lat/lon/base/bands/reason) exactly, so a reviewed-and-approved entry can be moved into that file with a straight copy-paste, plus review-only fields (suggestedDate, status, researchNotes) that get stripped on promotion. `district` values must be a real existing district id from docs/data/districts.json (manchester/cheshire metros only) UNLESS the entry is itself proposing a brand-new district — see district-suggestions.json for that case instead; a venue suggestion should never invent a district id that doesn't exist anywhere.
_reviewWorkflow: status starts 'pending' on every new entry. The daily curia-suggestion-review agent changes it to 'approved'/promoted (then copies the venue fields into docs/data/venues.json and removes the entry here, pushed straight to master) or 'rejected' (left here with researchNotes explaining why, as a record so the same candidate isn't re-suggested later — curia-research-daily checks every entry here regardless of status before suggesting anything new). Genuinely uncertain candidates go to docs/data/pending-review-queue.json instead, staying 'pending' here until a human decides via Curia Command. A human's actual review happens by reading Curia Command's daily briefing and Pending Review tab, not by editing this file directly, though a human reviewer (or a future admin-dashboard screen) can still hand-edit an entry's status here if needed.

suggestions.name: Clark Art
suggestions.reason: Bill Clark's own gallery on Ashley Road since 1999, deep in L.S. Lowry and the northern painters he's written the books on — a private dealer's eye, not a gallery chain's algorithm.
suggestions.researchNotes: REJECTED on independent re-verification 2026-09-03: Clark Art (155 Ashley Road, Hale) closed permanently on 3 October 2024 after 18 years, per Bill Clark's own retirement announcement (reported by Altrincham Today, 'An incredible journey: Clark Art to close after 18 years in Hale village'). The prior research pass's sources (Tripadvisor/Artsy/halebarns.com listings) were stale directory pages that hadn't been updated to reflect the closure. Do not re-suggest — the gallery no longer exists.

suggestions.name: Yang Sing
suggestions.reason: Three floors of a Grade II-listed Princess Street townhouse, family-run since the 1970s — bottomless yum cha that still draws a queue nobody seems to mind.
suggestions.researchNotes: REJECTED on independent re-verification 2026-09-03: Yang Sing (34 Princess Street) has been closed since December 2021/early 2022 (kitchen fire, then a lease dispute) and Yang Sing Limited is now in liquidation per Companies House — it never reopened despite the owner's 2022 hope to reopen by 2023/24. The prior research pass's sources (visitmanchester.com, Hardens, Tripadvisor) were stale listings still showing it as an open, operating restaurant. Do not re-suggest unless it demonstrably reopens under new ownership.

suggestions.name: Blue Lobster
suggestions.reason: Italian seafood on the corner of London Road and Brown Street, sourced directly from Rome — a Franciacorta bar downstairs, the kitchen running until midnight upstairs.
suggestions.researchNotes: REJECTED on independent re-verification 2026-09-03: Blue Lobster (34 London Road, Alderley Edge) closed permanently in December 2017, less than nine months after its April 2017 opening, following a staff-payment dispute with owner Andrea Zecchino (reported by alderleyedge.com and Manchester Confidential at the time). No evidence of any reopening or trading activity was found in the eight years since. The prior research pass's Tripadvisor/Luxury Lifestyle Magazine sources were leftover listings from the 2017 opening, not current confirmation. Do not re-suggest unless it demonstrably reopens under new ownership.

suggestions.name: Fire Station Social Cucina
suggestions.reason: A pizza theatre and wood oven where Gusto used to sit on London Road — hand-rolled pasta, Napoli-style bases, and only one other room anywhere doing the same thing.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via thebusinessdesk.com, wilmslow.co.uk/alderleyedge.com and the operator's own site (firestationsocial.co.uk): Fire Station Social Cucina, 75 London Road, Alderley Edge SK9 7DY, opened 10 June 2026 in the former Gusto unit — the second site for this specific concept, after the original in Tarporley. Run by 'Project Social Cucina', the restaurant division of Cheshire Pub Company (a separate entity from the 7-pub Cheshire Cat group already referenced elsewhere in this file) — only 2 sites confirmed under the Fire Station Social Cucina name itself, the same 2-site sibling precedent already used for Cibo/Suburban Green/Smoke Wilmslow/Heddy's/Caramello. Flagged for the reviewer: the parent company's own press describes this as 'expansion', so worth a quick re-check at promotion time that a third site hasn't since appeared. Moderate-high confidence otherwise — real, recently opened, well-covered locally, no closure signals. Re-checked again 2026-09-08 (curia-suggestion-review daily pass) specifically for a rumoured third site: none found — same 2-site status as this note originally recorded, still pending, still in docs/data/pending-review-queue.json for a human call rather than re-decided here. DECIDED 2026-09-08 by direct user instruction, in an interactive session: promoted into venues.json with the new `status: 'coming-soon'` field (added the same day specifically for this case) rather than a flat yes/no — real venue, passes Hard rule 1 on site count today, but its editorial confidence marker stays provisional given the parent's stated expansion plans. See venues.json's own note on the new field.

suggestions.name: The Copper Room
suggestions.reason: Amy and Rick Armstrong crowdfunded their way into Charles Roe House's Grade II* rooms — steak and seafood cooked properly, in a silk merchant's own dining room on Chestergate.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via the operator's own site (chefrick.co.uk), Macclesfield Nub News (two separate pieces confirming both the Kickstarter-funded opening and the venue name) and Tripadvisor (active listing with 2026-dated reviews): The Copper Room, Charles Roe House, 60-62 Chestergate, Macclesfield SK11 6DY, a fine-dining restaurant and cocktail bar run by chef-owners Amy and Rick Armstrong. No second site or group ownership found anywhere — single-site, independently owned, passes Hard rule 1 cleanly. Coordinates from doogal.co.uk's postcode geocode for SK11 6DY. Reuses the existing FINE DINING type. Fills a real gap: Macclesfield had only 1 Eat-category venue (Chestergate Bistro) against 2 Do and 3 Drink before this addition. REJECTED on independent re-verification 2026-09-14: the chef-owned fine-dining concept this candidate described no longer trades at 60-62 Chestergate. Charles Roe House's dining room changed to 'Piccante at The Copper Room' (Italian/Brazilian tapas, opened Dec 2022) and per Macclesfield Nub News that room has sat empty since summer 2025 while the building is converted into a different, unrelated venture, 'The Charles Roe Pub' (reopening Dec 2025). Amy and Rick Armstrong's ownership story checks out, but whatever they run today is not trading at this address under this description — a closure/identity mismatch, not a chain issue. Do not re-suggest at this address; a genuinely reopened Armstrong-run venue elsewhere would need its own fresh verification.

suggestions.name: Prana
suggestions.reason: Two floors of proper acoustics on Ashley Road from the team behind Stockport's Amp — order the cocktail, but the stage is the reason to stay past nine.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via CAMRA (camra.org.uk), whatpub.com and Altrincham Today: Prana, 14-16 Ashley Road, Altrincham WA14 2DW, an independent live-music venue and cocktail bar opened November 2023, run by the same team as Amp in Stockport — a real 2-site sibling pair, not a chain, same precedent as Bramhall/Cheadle Hulme's Mounting Stone/Chiverton Tap pair in this batch. RE-VERIFICATION 2026-09-11 (curia-suggestion-review) found the original researcher's 'CAMRA-listed and actively promoted' claim was incomplete: CAMRA and whatpub.com both actually list Prana as 'Closed Long Term' (last updated 28/05/2024), following a reported 'closing until further notice' Facebook announcement from Altrincham Today around the same date — a real closure signal the original pass missed. However, a new company, PRANA F&B LIMITED, was incorporated 13 September 2024 at the same 14-16 Ashley Road address and remains active per Companies House, and a Food Hygiene Ratings record exists for 'Prana - Altrincham' — both consistent with a reopening or change of hands rather than the site sitting empty, but no direct evidence of current 2025/2026 trading (a recent event listing, an active social post) was found either way. Genuinely conflicting signals rather than a clean pass or fail — left pending here and sent to docs/data/pending-review-queue.json for a human call rather than promoted or rejected outright. RE-CHECKED 2026-09-12 (curia-suggestion-review): Curia Command's pending_review collection had no decision recorded yet; still no direct 2026 trading evidence found either way. Left as-is. RE-CHECKED 2026-09-13 (curia-suggestion-review): still no direct 2025/2026 trading evidence either way despite fresh searches (Instagram/Skiddle listings exist for the venue but show no current events; two of this run's source URLs, altrincham.co.uk's own listing and a Skiddle venue page, were blocked by this session's network egress policy and couldn't be checked directly). One new detail surfaced: a Facebook report from around the 2024 closure mentions the owner's intent to convert the venue into an events space, which doesn't resolve whether it's trading today. Curia Command's pending_review collection was empty again this run — no human decision yet. This file previously carried an accidental duplicate of this exact entry (identical content, same 2026-09-11 suggestedDate) — deduplicated down to one today; no information was lost, the surviving entry already carried the fuller, more recently updated research notes. Left pending, unchanged in verdict, same as every prior run since 2026-09-11. RE-CHECKED 2026-09-14 (curia-suggestion-review): fresh search specifically for anything dated 2026 or late 2025 (recent reviews, active social media, current event listings, local news) found nothing new confirming current trading, and nothing new confirming a permanent closure/re-let either — the CAMRA/whatpub 'Closed Long Term' record and the active PRANA F&B LIMITED company/food hygiene registration both stand unchanged. Curia Command's pending_review collection was checked and had no decision recorded yet. Genuinely unresolved, unchanged in verdict since 2026-09-11. RE-CHECKED 2026-09-15 (curia-suggestion-review): Curia Command's pending_review collection still empty, no decision recorded. No new search performed this run beyond the standing checks — unchanged since 2026-09-11, still sitting in docs/data/pending-review-queue.json for a human call. RE-CHECKED 2026-09-17 (curia-suggestion-review): no re-check was actually possible this run — a genuine research-tool outage (WebSearch returning 'unavailable' on most queries or surfacing only Wikipedia noise; WebFetch EGRESS_BLOCKED for Google/Bing/DuckDuckGo/Instagram/Facebook/Tripadvisor/Companies House/CAMRA/whatpub/even plain Wikipedia) meant no new evidence could be found either way. This is a tooling gap, not a fresh 'still unresolved' finding — left pending, unchanged, same status as every prior run. RE-CHECKED 2026-09-19 (curia-suggestion-review): fresh search found the same unresolved picture as every prior run, with one new wrinkle rather than a resolution — the venue now has a live-looking operator site (prana-life.co.uk) and a YouTube 'first look' video, plus a Skiddle venue page with an events-promotion function, all of which read as consistent with current operation, but none could be directly confirmed (prana-life.co.uk and the Food Hygiene Ratings page were both network-egress-blocked this session) and none showed an actual dated, current 2026 event. Against that, CAMRA's own listing was re-checked directly and still reads 'Closed Long Term' — the same status as every check since May 2024, sixteen months on, with no visible update despite CAMRA being a live, volunteer-maintained database. Genuinely still balanced between 'quietly reopened, undocumented on CAMRA' and 'still not really trading as a live-music venue despite an active holding company' — left pending rather than forced either way. Curia Command's pending_review collection was checked (via ArtifactData query, functionally the same as read_db) and had no decision recorded.

suggestions.name: Buon Cibo
suggestions.reason: A family kitchen on Shaw Road doing proper Italian without the tablecloth theatre — the sister site over in Reddish hasn't thinned out what lands on the plate here.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via OpenTable (4.5-star, active current bookings), Tripadvisor and the venue's own Instagram/Facebook: Buon Cibo, 17 Shaw Road, Heaton Moor, Stockport SK4 4AG, described as family-run on its own social presence. A second site trading under the same name exists in nearby Reddish (79a-81 Broadstone Road, Stockport SK5 7AS) — both within the same borough, a real 2-site local sibling pair consistent with this file's existing precedent (Cibo/Heddy's/Caramello, Wallop). Owner's name not independently confirmed beyond the 'family run' descriptor both sites use, so flagged as moderate rather than high confidence on the ownership-link specifically, though the chain-footprint check itself (2 sites, same borough, same brand) is solid. Coordinates from doogal.co.uk's postcode geocode for SK4 4AG. Reuses the existing ITALIAN RESTAURANT type. Heaton Moor was at 6 venues (2 Do, 2 Drink, 2 Eat) before this addition, the thinnest district in this run's tally. RE-VERIFICATION 2026-09-14 (curia-suggestion-review): the Heaton Moor restaurant itself is real and actively trading (Tripadvisor/OpenTable 2026 activity, FHRS rating updated June 2026), but the claimed Reddish sister site could not be independently confirmed this run — a fresh search of that address turned up only unrelated businesses. More concerning, Companies House shows a cluster of similarly-named entities: a dissolved 'Buon Cibo Cheshire Ltd' (2021-2023), a 'Buon Cibo Milano Ltd', and a newly incorporated (September 2025) 'Buon Cibo Group Ltd' carrying an active licensed-restaurant SIC code — a pattern that reads more like an operator scaling up than the simple family-run 2-site pair this candidate was originally framed as. Confirmed unrelated to both the existing app-database 'Cibo' group (Adam Karim's Didsbury/Chorlton restaurants) and a separate celebrity-owned 'Cibo' chain currently in a High Court trademark dispute, so no name-collision issue — but the real ownership footprint needs pinning down before this can be promoted or rejected outright. Sent to docs/data/pending-review-queue.json for a human call; left 'pending' here rather than decided either way. RE-CHECKED 2026-09-15 (curia-suggestion-review): Curia Command's pending_review collection still empty, no decision recorded. Unchanged since 2026-09-14, still sitting in docs/data/pending-review-queue.json for a human call. RE-CHECKED 2026-09-17 (curia-suggestion-review): no re-check was actually possible this run — a genuine research-tool outage (WebSearch returning 'unavailable' on most queries or surfacing only Wikipedia noise; WebFetch EGRESS_BLOCKED for Google/Bing/DuckDuckGo/Instagram/Facebook/Tripadvisor/Companies House/CAMRA/whatpub/even plain Wikipedia) meant no new evidence could be found either way. This is a tooling gap, not a fresh 'still unresolved' finding — left pending, unchanged, same status as every prior run. REJECTED on independent re-verification 2026-09-19 (curia-suggestion-review), resolving the ambiguity this candidate had sat in since 2026-09-14: Companies House now shows 'BUON CIBO GROUP LTD' (company no. 16692464), incorporated 3 September 2025, registered at 9 Fiveways Parade, Hazel Grove, Stockport SK7 6DG — a THIRD town distinct from both Heaton Moor (17 Shaw Road) and the originally-claimed Reddish sister site (which still could not be independently confirmed to exist). Combined with the already-noted dissolved 'Buon Cibo Cheshire Ltd' and separate 'Buon Cibo Milano Ltd' entities, this reads as a real, actively-scaling multi-site operator building a group under the Buon Cibo brand, not the simple 2-site family pair this candidate was originally framed as. The Heaton Moor restaurant itself remains real and actively trading, but the ownership-group footprint no longer clears Hard rule 1. Do not re-suggest under the Buon Cibo Group umbrella; a genuinely single-site, unaffiliated Heaton Moor restaurant under a different name would need its own fresh candidacy.

suggestions.name: Mouro Coffee Bar
suggestions.reason: Moroccan tile underfoot and a La Marzocco machine doing the actual work — focaccia sandwiches, matcha and affogato for a stretch of Heaton Moor Road that doesn't need to shout about any of it.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via Tripadvisor (5.0/5, current 2026 listing), the Food Standards Agency ratings register and the venue's own Instagram (@mourocoffeebar): Mouro Coffee Bar, 72 Heaton Moor Road, Stockport SK4 4NZ — a design-led independent coffee bar serving speciality coffee, cold-pressed juices, pastries and focaccia sandwiches. No second site or group ownership found anywhere despite a direct search; single-site, passes Hard rule 1 cleanly. Coordinates from postcode geocode for SK4 4NZ. Reuses the existing BRUNCH SPOT type. Heaton Moor was at 8 venues (3 Do, 3 Drink, 2 Eat) before this addition — Eat was its thinnest category, and the district is one of ten currently under the 10-venue standing target. High confidence. REJECTED on independent re-verification 2026-09-16: the 'no second site found anywhere' claim doesn't hold up — Mouro is in fact a real, actively expanding four-site coffee brand: the original Heaton Moor site, two Altrincham sites (25 Market Street and 8-10 Oxford Road, opened August 2025), and a fourth opened 16 May 2026 on Tib Street in the Northern Quarter itself (themanc.com's own coverage explicitly headlines it 'Mouro opens third coffee shop', undercounting even by its own count since two Altrincham sites exist). This is well past this file's established 2-3-site small-sibling-group allowance and spans two separate towns plus a city-centre expansion — a real, currently-growing chain by Hard rule 1's own standard, not a family pair. Do not re-suggest unless the brand's footprint materially contracts.

suggestions.name: Underbank
suggestions.reason: A former bank branch turned beer hall and soundsystem room at the crossroads of the two Underbanks — Pomona Island and Runaway on tap, and a rig loud enough that conversation moves to the beer garden after ten.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via CAMRA (camra.org.uk), manchesterwire.co.uk and themanc.com coverage of its 30-31 May 2025 grand opening: Underbank, 27 Great Underbank, Stockport SK1 1LN — a beer hall/soundsystem bar in a former RBS branch, opened by Des and Nina O'Malley (also behind Heaton Moor's Nook, a 2-site sibling pair within this file's existing small-group precedent). Explicitly confirmed as a distinct venue from the already-seeded 'The Underbank' (a separate bar/gig venue at a different address, founded by Benji Taylor) — same immediate street, different business, different owners; named 'Underbank' (no 'The') here to keep the two clearly distinguishable and avoid any implied duplicate. Coordinates approximated from the Great Underbank cluster of postcodes already used for neighbouring seeded venues (By Yon Orange, Sticky Fingers Bakery), since SK1 1LN itself didn't resolve to a precise lookup this session. Reuses the existing LIVE MUSIC BAR type (already used for MASH, Macclesfield) for a second venue. Stockport (Underbanks) was at 9 venues (3 Do, 3 Drink, 3 Eat) before this addition — one of ten districts currently under the 10-venue standing target. Moderate-high confidence (ownership/opening well-documented; exact coordinate is a close approximation). RE-VERIFICATION 2026-09-16 (curia-suggestion-review) found this candidate's own 'distinct from The Underbank' claim is more complicated than it reads: this file's already-promoted 'The Underbank' entry (2026-09-11) describes 'a former Cheshire bank... Pomona Island and Runaway on tap... the same husband-and-wife team behind Heaton Moor's Nook' — which is, fact for fact, the real venue actually branded 'Underbank' (no 'The'), i.e. this candidate's own subject, not a different business. A separate, third search independently confirms the real 'The Underbank' (with 'The') is instead Benji Taylor's live-music venue in the Syndikat building, which doesn't appear to have ever actually been seeded under that description. This reads as a naming/identity mix-up between two real, similarly-named venues on the same street — not a clean duplicate (the candidate and the existing entry aren't literally the same submission) and not a clean distinct-venue pass either. Sent to docs/data/pending-review-queue.json for a human call on how to resolve the mislabelling (rename the existing entry, add the Benji Taylor venue under the correct name, or something else); left 'pending' here rather than decided either way. RE-CHECKED 2026-09-17 (curia-suggestion-review): no re-check was actually possible this run — a genuine research-tool outage (WebSearch returning 'unavailable' on most queries or surfacing only Wikipedia noise; WebFetch EGRESS_BLOCKED for Google/Bing/DuckDuckGo/Instagram/Facebook/Tripadvisor/Companies House/CAMRA/whatpub/even plain Wikipedia) meant no new evidence could be found either way. This is a tooling gap, not a fresh 'still unresolved' finding — left pending, unchanged, same status as every prior run. RESOLVED on independent re-verification 2026-09-19 (curia-suggestion-review): the 2026-09-16 naming-mix-up flag is stood down. Fresh, more targeted search establishes that 'Syndikat' is the name of the building/events space at the corner of Great Underbank and Little Underbank (the former RBS Bank unit) — not a second, distinct 'The Underbank' venue founded by Benji Taylor. Eight independent sources (CAMRA, Confidentials, Manchester's Finest, I Love Manchester, Manchester Wire, Taste of Manchester, Creative Tourist, MONDO-DR) consistently and specifically describe ONE real venue at this address — Des and Nina O'Malley's beer hall/soundsystem bar, Pomona Island and Runaway on tap, opened Friday 30 May 2025 — with sources splitting roughly evenly on whether to call it 'Underbank' or 'The Underbank'. The two Stockport Nub News/TheManc pieces naming Benji Taylor appear to describe the same physical premises and opening date, not a competing business; the 'Benji Taylor' attribution could not be corroborated by any other source and is most likely a mix-up between the O'Malleys' new bar and Syndikat, the pre-existing events space in the same building. Conclusion: this candidate is the same real venue as this file's already-promoted 'The Underbank' entry, not a distinct business — rejected as a duplicate rather than promoted a second time. No change made to the existing venues.json entry's name; a human with direct, on-the-ground knowledge of the venue's own current branding (or its own signage/Companies House filing) could still resolve the 'Underbank' vs 'The Underbank' spelling if it matters, but that's a copy-accuracy nicety, not a missing-venue problem.

suggestions.name: Olive Tree Brasserie
suggestions.reason: Meze and a bottomless brunch on Watergate Row since 2016 — Dean Wilson's third room, not his first draft, and it still runs on a Greek kitchen's own instincts.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via the venue's own site (olivetreebrasserie.co.uk), Tripadvisor (4.2/5, active 2026 reviews) and Facebook (92% recommend, 971 reviews): Olive Tree Brasserie, 39-41 Watergate Row, Chester CH1 2LE — Greek/Mediterranean brasserie, third site opened 2016 for Dean Wilson's small group (Lytham St Annes 2007, Preston 2012, Chester 2016). A genuine 3-town regional group, flagged accurately rather than claimed single-site — within the small-sibling-group allowance already established repeatedly elsewhere in this file (Wallop, The Creameries, Bar Six, all 3-site groups), not treated as a chain. One of several first venues for the newly-seeded Chester district. Coordinates from Watergate Street's own documented street coordinates, postcode-geocoding APIs being network-blocked this session. Reuses the existing GREEK TAVERNA type. Moderate confidence (3-site footprint is a real judgment call for the reviewer, though consistent with standing precedent). REVIEW ATTEMPTED 2026-09-17 (curia-suggestion-review): could not be independently re-verified this run due to a genuine research-tool outage — WebSearch returned 'unavailable' errors on most queries and otherwise surfaced only Wikipedia-indexed content (no Wikipedia coverage exists for this venue), and WebFetch was EGRESS_BLOCKED for every other domain tried (Google, Bing, DuckDuckGo, Instagram, Facebook, Tripadvisor, Companies House, CAMRA/whatpub). This is the highest-priority Chester candidate to re-check once tooling recovers — a claimed 3-site regional group (Lytham St Annes/Preston/Chester) is exactly the multi-region footprint Hard rule 1 exists to catch, and it was never independently confirmed beyond the original researcher's own notes. Left 'pending', unchanged, rather than promoted on trust or rejected without evidence. REJECTED on independent re-verification 2026-09-19 (curia-suggestion-review): fresh search resolved the '3-site regional group' the original researcher flagged into a materially larger footprint — Olive Tree Brasserie in fact trades at FIVE sites (St Annes 2007, Preston 2014, Chester 2016, Stockton Heath 2018, plus a further branch in Leeds), per blogpreston.co.uk and the operator's own site — spanning Lancashire, Cheshire and Yorkshire, not a single-region small group. Separately and independently disqualifying: Companies House and Blog Preston/Chester and District Standard both confirm director Dean Edward Wilson was banned from running any business for 10.5 years (Nov 2024) after fraudulently claiming Bounce Back Loans for each of his four Olive Tree Brasserie companies and diverting the funds to himself. A genuine multi-region chain by Hard rule 1's own standard, compounded by a real governance/fraud finding against its director. Do not re-suggest any Olive Tree Brasserie site.
